verdict.rationale: Clerky documents a Partner API that creates document sets from templates (`POST /v1/document_sets`), returns forms with JSON schemas, accepts submitted JSON values, and exposes lifecycle state for polling, so generate and populate are first-party. Its scope and readiness are limited: it covers only Delaware C-Corp formations, OAuth access is 'coming soon' ahead of partner launch, and signing and sending happen on Clerky rather than through the API. Missing for 10: API-driven sending/signature dispatch, document types beyond Delaware C-Corp formation, generally available authentication, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can generate, populate, and send legal documents programmatically through a documented API

citations.quote: Your product creates a document set, renders the forms the API returns, submits JSON values, and polls for lifecycle state.
It currently supports Delaware C-Corporation formations.
Create a document set from a template.
OAuth-based access is coming soon; client registration, URLs, scopes, token lifetime, and refresh behavior will be published before partner integrations launch.
